core_obligations: Reduce the whole list to a first order thickening on an affine chart: the base change direction is uniform for all clauses, the converse is handled by induction on the order of S in S' using the filtration of the definition discussion, and then an affine open U' = Spec(A') of S' with an affine open V' = Spec(B') of X' over it is used to write V' cap X = Spec(B'/IB'), A = A'/I, B = B'/IB' and a commutative diagram with exact rows and I^2 = 0 (proof lines 357-400).

Settle the clauses that become algebra on that chart: surjectivity of A to B lifts to A' to B' by Nakayama, finite typeness is lifted along a surjection A'[x_1,...,x_n] to B', quasi-finiteness and relative dimension d follow from the fibrewise criteria, Omega_{B/A} = Omega_{B'/A'}/I Omega_{B'/A'} is used with Nakayama and the fact that Omega_{B'/A'} is a finite B'-module to get clause (5), and unramifiedness combines that vanishing with finite typeness (proof lines 402-437).

Settle the clauses that are not translations of the chart algebra: clauses (7) and (8) combine finite typeness with the earlier thickening lemma and the structure of proper and of finite morphisms; clause (9) applies the clauses already proved to the morphism of thickenings from X in X' to X times_S X in X' times_{S'} X', obtains that X' to X' times_{S'} X' is a closed immersion whose ideal sits inside the pullback of the ideal cutting out S in S', and concludes with the diagonal criterion and clause (5); clause (10) factors f into an open immersion followed by a closed immersion, lifts the open subscheme U of S to the open subscheme U' of S' with the same underlying space and applies clause (1) (proof lines 439-473).
proof_roadmap: Uniform easy direction: every property listed is stable under base change, and f is the base change of f' along X = S times_{S'} X', so only the converse needs work (proof lines 357-375).

Reduction to first order and to an affine chart: induction on the order of the thickening reduces to I^2 = 0, and a chosen affine open U' of S' with an affine open V' of X' over it produces the exact commutative diagram of A', B', A and B with I^2 = 0 (proof lines 376-400).

Algebraic clauses: Nakayama for (1) and (2) and for (5), the fibrewise criteria for (3) and (4), and the combination of finite typeness with the vanishing of the differentials for (6) (proof lines 402-437).
Clauses (7) and (8): finite typeness plus the earlier thickening lemma plus the usual descriptions of proper and of finite morphisms (proof lines 439-449).

Clauses (9) and (10): the diagonal trick for monomorphisms, where the ideal of the closed immersion X' to X' times_{S'} X' is shown to sit inside the pullback of the ideal of S in S', and the factorisation of an immersion through an open subscheme lifted from S to S' (proof lines 451-473).
difficulty_reason: The counted statement collects eleven clauses asserting that a morphism f : X to S and its thickening f' : X' to S' have the same behaviour with respect to closed immersions, local finite typeness, local quasi-finiteness, relative dimension d, vanishing of differentials, unramifiedness, properness, finiteness, being a monomorphism and being an immersion, under the hypothesis that X = S times_{S'} X' and that S in S' is a finite order thickening (statement lines 336-354). One direction is pure base change, so the work is the converse, and it is a chain rather than a citation: the proof reduces first to a first order thickening by the filtration of the definition discussion, then to an affine chart on which the problem becomes a statement about A to B and A' to B' with I^2 = 0, and it settles the clauses one by one using Nakayama three separate times, the fibrewise criteria for quasi-finiteness and relative dimension, and finite generation of Omega_{B'/A'} (proof lines 376-437). Clauses (9) and (10) are not translations of the chart algebra: the monomorphism clause is proved by running the already established clauses on the thickening of the diagonal and then computing that the conormal sheaf of X' to X' times_{S'} X' vanishes, and the immersion clause by lifting an open subscheme of S to an open subscheme of S' with the same underlying space (proof lines 451-473).
